newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-DESERT KING BOUNCES BACK TO WIN IRISH DERBY.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DESERT KING BOUNCES BACK TO WIN IRISH DERBY.

text.p: Desert King, ridden by veteran Christy Roche, put a major Royal Ascot failure firmly behind him to win the Irish Derby at The Curragh on Sunday.
The colt, trained by Aidan O'Brien, had won the Irish 2,000 Guineas earlier in the season only to fail at Ascot in the St James's Palace Stakes, finishing fourth behind Starborough.

But his undoubted class shone through over a longer distance. Roche brought the 11-2 chance home a length clear of Dr Johnson (12-1), ridden by Johnny Murtagh, with French raider Loup Sauvage (8-1) a short head away in third place.
The big disappointment was English challenger Silver Patriarch, the 5-4 favourite, who finished a well beaten fifth in the 10-strong field.
Silver Patriarch had been edged out by a short head by Benny The Dip in the Epsom Derby where he was considered an unlucky loser after racing in last place with five furlongs (1-km) left.
On Sunday, jockey Pat Eddery cut out the pace with The Fly, the other English raider, but turning into the straight it was clear both were going to struggle.
Dr Johnson surged through to take up the running with 300 metres to go only to be cut down in the closing stages by Desert King who held on readily.
Trainer O'Brien, who also saddled Johan Cruyff (fourth) and Strawberry Roan (eighth) in Sunday's race, has now won all three Irish classics to be raced so far this season.
Desert King's success provided significant consolation for ex-bookmaker Michael Tabor who also owns Entrepreneur, a disappointing fourth in the Epsom Derby.
